cells.tense: The inner scale sits level right now as you read it and it reads back.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take a finishing that stayed with you — a role, a season, a way you used to run things — and add up the yield side only. What it grew, freed, handed over. Once through.
cells.core:
You feel what's fair before you argue it. Standing where the shared way gets set, you can tell what a piece of work is owed, what a person is owed, and you set it down without running the calculation twice. It arrives whole, and it holds while things press on it.

Something ended in your care a while back and you haven't taken its inventory. Before the next arrangement gets built, sit with that ending and count what it left behind — the skill it forced, the room it opened, the thing it handed you that you'd have turned down otherwise. Your reckoning is a harvest account too, not just a bill. Draw it once, honestly, and the next pattern you set will come from a fuller hand.

cells.tense: The scale will be run on outcomes that haven't happened yet and can't be written in.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Choose a person inside this arrangement and put something solid under them — an hour, a call, a piece of your standing — then close it. Don't check how they used it.
cells.core:
You are weighing consequences that haven't arrived. The arrangement isn't even built, and each person's share is already getting weighed in your hands, checked and rechecked for how fair it'll look once it lands. It feels like care from where you sit. From across the table it's a verdict handed down early — people can feel themselves measured before they've moved.

Your strength is real, and right now it's pinning things that need to move. Set that strength under a person instead of over them. Hand over something concrete, and once it's handed, leave it. A structure holds what it can contain without pressing. Put down what you're carrying for them, and the fairness you're guarding gets to arrive when it arrives, which is the only time it can.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door the shared way already closed behind you.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Walk beside a person through a stretch that's familiar ground to you — the whole stretch, at their pace — and when it opens out, stop. Let them carry it from there.
cells.core:
A pattern here ended, or should have, and you've stayed at its edge. Your sense of what's fair went quiet about your own place in it. What each other person is owed still comes clear to you, easily, and your own share won't come into your hand. The structure you're good at is standing with a room missing, and you're standing in that room.

What you do have is ground you covered before, with its turns in view. Go with the one who's on it now — not ahead, alongside — and when it opens out, let go of the walking. Saying the passage as you cover it brings it back into view, and your own place comes back when you stop vouching for theirs.

cells.tense: Your hand is off the pen in a room you're still quietly setting for people.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Put every tug on you on paper — all of them — then make a mark beside the ones you'd still carry if no one were watching. Nothing else. The marks are the work.
cells.core:
You are the one who settles how things get shared here, and your hand is in that ledger everywhere. Asked, you'd say the arrangement is simply what's fair — the pattern is just what it is. But the terms people live inside keep coming from your read on what's owed, and they hold because you're still holding them.

That sense wore so smooth you stopped hearing it as a choice you make. Here's the plainer question: of the pulls on you now, how many came from someone else's expectation? Put them all down, then mark the ones you would carry if no one were watching for it. What's marked is your own compass, and it reads clean without the borrowed weight once you can see which debts you didn't sign.
